template:
Hi,

Noticed you do {{business_type}} around {{city}}.

We can book you 10 qualified {{inspection_type}} that turn into paid {{project_type}} jobs, in under 30 days.

You only pay when I book you a qualified, confirmed {{inspection_singular}}.

Open to a 15-minute chat?

instructions.business_type: the trade this company leads with on its own website, lowercase, EXACTLY one of: solar and battery storage, home battery storage, solar pv, heat pumps and solar, renewable energy installs. Use the one the site LEADS with (hero line, page title, first service listed). Map: solar panels + battery / solar & storage / PV and battery -> solar and battery storage; battery storage / home batteries / backup power / Powerwall / GivEnergy battery -> home battery storage; solar panels only, no battery mentioned -> solar pv; air source heat pumps first, solar second -> heat pumps and solar; a firm that lists solar, batteries, EV chargers and heat pumps as one bundle with no lead trade -> renewable energy installs. Never any other phrase, NEVER 'generator', NEVER 'electrical services', and never a US label ('solar contractor', 'energy storage systems').
instructions.inspection_type: the FIRST VISIT to a homeowner, plural, UK usage: ALWAYS 'home energy surveys' for every business_type — a UK homeowner books a survey, not an inspection, an estimate or a quote. If the company's own site consistently calls the first visit 'site survey' or 'home survey', you may use 'home surveys'. NEVER 'free'. NEVER 'inspection', 'estimate', 'quote' or 'consultation'. NEVER the whole business_type phrase inside this value.
instructions.inspection_singular: the singular of inspection_type: 'home energy survey' (or 'home survey' when that variant was used). It reads after 'a qualified, confirmed', so it must be one bookable thing.
instructions.project_type: the OUTCOME NOUN the homeowner pays for, reading immediately before the word 'jobs'. By business_type: solar and battery storage -> solar and battery; home battery storage -> battery; solar pv -> solar; heat pumps and solar -> heat pump and solar; renewable energy installs -> install. Never plural, never 'project', 'system' or 'installation'.
instructions.city: ONLY if the 'city' known fact is blank: the UK town or city this company is based in, read from the website. Give the TOWN, never the county or a region or a service-area phrase. Use a county name ONLY when the site names no town at all. Otherwise repeat the known city exactly.

rules: Decide business_type first — EXACTLY one of the five allowed trades, the one the site leads with — then derive inspection_type, inspection_singular and project_type from the tables above; do not invent a sixth combination. No single word may appear in ALL THREE of business_type, inspection_type and project_type (that is why the visit noun is 'home energy surveys' for every trade: 'battery surveys' + 'home battery storage' + 'battery' would trip flag_word_used_3x), and inspection_type must never contain the whole business_type phrase. Never 'free' in inspection_type. UK spelling and vocabulary throughout. No company gets 'generator' — this is the battery / solar list, not the generator list.

_r._: OPERATOR NOTES — not instructions to the personalisation subagent. DRAFT 2026-09-30 for the MCS battery-installer list (option A of ICP-generators-uk.md); derived from personalize-config-uk.json (foundation repair) and NOT yet signed off. Nothing is filled at full volume until the 3-lead and 7-lead tests below are approved.
_r.offer: The US offer line ('10 qualified generator estimate appointments') becomes 'We can book you 10 qualified home energy surveys that turn into paid solar and battery jobs, in under 30 days.' Average installed job (web-checked 2026-09-30): £3,500–£8,500 battery-only, £10k–£15k with solar — the line is credible for this trade.
_r.business_type: Five values from what the register + site text actually show: 2,198 of 2,794 installers are battery+solar, 577 also do heat pumps, 15 are battery-only. 'renewable energy installs' is the catch-all for the bundle sites (solar / battery / EV / heat pump with no lead trade) so the reader never invents a sixth label. 'generator' is banned outright — a leftover from the sibling list would be the clearest tell.
_r.inspection_type: One visit noun for every trade on purpose. The UK solar/battery trade's first visit IS a home survey (sometimes 'home energy survey' / 'site survey'); a per-trade table would put 'battery' or 'solar' into all three values and trip flag_word_used_3x on most of the list. 'free' is banned — 'free home survey' is the phrase the whole trade already spams.
_r.project_type: The thing the homeowner pays for, reading before 'jobs': 'paid solar and battery jobs', 'paid battery jobs', 'paid heat pump and solar jobs'. 'install' only for the bundle firms.
_r.context_cols: 'technologies' (from the register: battery|solar pv|ashp…) is added so the reader can pick heat-pump-led vs solar-led when the site text is thin; 'state' stays out (UK).
_r.registry_only_rows: 1,231 leads have NO site text (register email only). They fill on the fallbacks — 'solar and battery storage around <city>' — which is true for 79% of the register. The operator decides whether these send; report `fallback_only` before upload as always.

_test_plan: OPERATOR NOTE — per SKILL STEP 7b. (1) THREE-LEAD TEST: one solar-and-battery lead, one heat-pump-led lead, one home-battery-storage lead; one subagent over a 3-item batch; read the three emails to the operator — voice check ('home energy surveys', 'paid battery jobs'). (2) SEVEN-LEAD TEST: cover all five trades, one brand-family branch (Project Solar / Heatable / Sunsave), one blank-city lead, one registry-only lead (no site text) so the fallback row is seen as it will ship; run `fill` and read fill_report.json: expect 0 flag_visit_repeats_trade, 0 flag_word_used_3x, 0 flag_free_in_visit, 0 flag_outcome_off_trade (live here via outcome_by_type). (3) FULL FILL only after both sign-offs: prep -> one Haiku per batch -> fill -> redo loop -> check --csv; report fallback_only and blank_city before any upload.
